prayerExcerpt.en-US: Each year may bring us fresh changes and trials; let us learn from St. Fulgentius to receive all that happens as from the hand of God, and appointed for our salvation.
prayerExcerpt.pt-BR: Cada ano pode trazer-nos novas mudanças e provações; aprendamos com São Fulgêncio a receber tudo o que acontece como vindo da mão de Deus, e ordenado para a nossa salvação.

meta.face: A North African of about sixty-five with a warm olive-brown complexion and a SHORT, BROAD face, as wide at the flat cheekbones as it is long — a broad, rounded forehead running up into a BALD crown with a ring of close-cropped grey-black curls above the ears, a short, wide nose with a low, flat bridge and broad nostrils, large, round, dark-brown eyes set wide apart under thick, straight grey-black brows, full lips, a short, rounded chin; a full, short, grizzled grey beard trimmed close to the jaw; a mild, patient gaze toward us.
meta.basis: The seventeenth-century portrait on Wikipedia (Fulgentius of Ruspe) shows him bald with a fringe, a full greying beard, a black habit and a white pallium with a crozier and book; the card keeps those marks. His African birth (Telepte, in today's Tunisia) gives the complexion, and the island monastery where the book says he spent his last year gives the setting. Kept apart from `augustine` (close-cropped dark hair, short dark beard) by the bald crown, the grizzled beard and the short, flat-cheeked face.
